symptoms: You may see brown egg masses near the tips of the leaves.
The caterpillar bores into the center of the shoot and the tiller.
The central shoot dries up and is called a dead heart.
In older plants, the whole panicle dries up and turns white, which is called a white ear.
Affected plants can be pulled out of the ground easily by hand.
prevention: Clip the tips of seedlings before you transplant them to remove egg masses.
Choose rice varieties that are resistant or moderately resistant to the borer.
After harvest, till the soil and flood the field to destroy larvae hiding in the stubble.
Delay planting times to avoid the peak time when moths come out.
Use seedbeds as a trap crop for moths.
practices: Collect and destroy any egg masses you find in the main field.
Use pheromone traps to monitor the number of moths in your field.
Use light traps in the evening to observe the pests.
Use sweep nets to check the population of pests and their natural enemies.
